---
emoji: "🆕"
name: "Weekly What's New"
description: Opens a PR to update the What's New page
private: true

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: weekly on sunday

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: read
  pull-requests: read
  copilot-requests: write

model: opus
engine:
  id: copilot
  copilot-sdk: true
max-tool-denials: 3
strict: true

sandbox:
  agent:
    sudo: false

tracker-id: generate-whats-new

network:
  allowed:
    - defaults
    - github

safe-outputs:
  create-pull-request:
    expires: 6d
    draft: false
    protected-files: blocked
    reviewers: [ckittel]
    assignees: [ckittel]
    max: 1
    if-no-changes: warn
    allowed-files:
      - docs/changelog.md
      - docs/feed.atom
    max-patch-files: 2
    signed-commits: true

tools:
  cli-proxy: true
  github:
    mode: gh-proxy
    toolsets: [default]
  edit:
  bash: true

timeout-minutes: 15
---

# Update AAC's "What's New" page

Review pull requests merged in the last seven days and create a PR that updates the "What's New" page (`docs/changelog.md`) with a summary of what articles changed. The PR also needs to update the RSS feed that goes with that page (`docs/feed.atom`).

- You're the sole generator of these two files; no other script maintains them. Keep the autogenerated notice in `docs/changelog.md` intact.

- Update the `changelog.md` file's `ms.date` front matter to the date you generate the page. Only do this when you're already making content changes to the page. Never bump `ms.date` on its own, because a date change alone must not trigger a PR.

- Use the style from the current page to guide how you add new entries or update existing entries.

- The page only keeps a rolling history. Keep the four most recent months. When a new month begins, remove the oldest month that rolls off, along with its RSS feed entries.

- When an article is renamed as part of an update, don't count that article as new. This rule applies to articles that go from .yml -> .md conversion or vice versa, in addition to simple file renames.

- When linking to commits, link to the `architecture-center` mirror, not the `architecture-center-pr` repo. Both repos share the same commit SHAs, so reuse the same SHA in the mirror URL.

- In `docs/feed.atom`, use each article's `description` front matter as the entry's `<summary>`.

- For the Atom RSS feed, validate that your XML syntax is correct. For example, run `xmllint --noout docs/feed.atom`.

- Use the "Sentence case" version of the article's title, not the "Book Title" case.

- Exclude files from the changelog if the changes are "minor". This condition is true if the changes are any combination of the following conditions:
  - An article only got touched because of URL updates (an article it linked to now got changed to a new URL).
  - An article only had metadata changed.

- If nothing qualifies for an update entry, don't open a PR. Call the `noop` tool with a message that explains why: `{"noop": {"message": "No action needed: [brief explanation]"}}`.
